title: About
text:
I am a Professor at the University of British Columbia and Canada Research Chair in Ocean Sustainability and Global Change. My research examines how climate change is transforming marine ecosystems, fisheries, aquatic food systems, and ocean-dependent societies.
I develop interdisciplinary models, scenarios, and assessments to understand climate risks and identify pathways toward sustainable, equitable, and resilient ocean futures. My work spans research, training, knowledge mobilization, and international science-policy assessments, including the IPCC and IPBES.

title: Leadership
text:
Scientific leadership is about creating the conditions for excellent research that advances knowledge and helps address societal challenges. It involves fostering inclusive and collaborative environments where diverse perspectives, disciplines, and ways of knowing come together to generate innovative solutions for complex ocean sustainability issues. Effective leadership enables individuals and teams to thrive, supports creativity and innovation, builds research capacity, and strengthens the connections between science and society.
Throughout my career, I have sought to build interdisciplinary teams, develop international partnerships, mentor the next generation of researchers, and bridge science, policy, and practice. My approach is grounded in collaboration, integrity, inclusion, and shared purpose, with the goal of advancing scientific excellence while generating knowledge that informs decisions and contributes to a more sustainable and equitable future.

title: Research
text:
The ocean is changing rapidly under the combined pressures of climate change, direct exploitation, habitat change, pollution and invasive species. My research seeks to understand how these drivers interact to shape marine ecosystems and the societies that depend on them. I combine observations, ecological theory, numerical modelling, and participatory approaches with insights from the economic and social sciences to generate knowledge that supports sustainable ocean management, climate adaptation, biodiversity conservation, and resilient blue food systems.
My work spans four interconnected research themes.

title: Training & Mentoring
text:
Training the next generation of scientists is one of the most rewarding aspects of my academic career.
I strive to create a research environment where curiosity, collaboration, scientific excellence, and mutual respect enable students and postdoctoral researchers to develop into independent scholars and future leaders. My mentoring philosophy emphasizes intellectual growth, interdisciplinary thinking, effective communication, and research that contributes to society.

title: Knowledge Mobilization
text:
Excellent science has its greatest impact when it informs decisions.
My research is designed not only to advance scientific understanding but also to support governments, Indigenous communities, industry, non-governmental organizations, and international bodies in addressing the challenges facing the ocean. I work closely with partners throughout the research process to ensure that scientific evidence is relevant, accessible, and useful for policy and practice.

title: About

Research approach
My work connects marine ecology, fisheries science, climate-impact assessment, economics, scenarios, and governance. I am particularly interested in understanding how changes in ocean conditions interact with biodiversity, food systems, institutions, and societal choices.
A central goal of my research is to produce knowledge that is scientifically rigorous, useful for stakeholders, right-holders and decision-making, and attentive to sustainability and equity.

title: Research
text:
Climate Change and Marine Ecosystems
Climate change is fundamentally reshaping marine ecosystems through ocean warming, marine heatwaves, ocean acidification, deoxygenation, sea-level rise, and changes in ocean circulation. My research examines how these drivers alter species distributions, ecosystem productivity, food-web dynamics, ecosystem services, and fisheries and aquaculture across regional and global scales. I develop and apply interdisciplinary modelling approaches that integrate ecological, environmental, economic, and social dimensions to project future changes, identify emerging risks, evaluate adaptation and conservation strategies, and explore alternative scenarios for sustainable ocean futures.
Representative topics: marine heatwaves, species redistribution, ecosystem modelling, ecosystem services, ocean acidification, deoxygenation, future scenarios, climate adaptation.

title: Research
text:
Blue Food Futures
Marine fisheries and aquaculture play essential roles in food security, nutrition, livelihoods, and economic development. My research explores how climate change and other environmental pressures influence the future of blue foods, and how governance, technology, and policy can enhance resilience and equity. This work integrates ecological, economic, and social dimensions to identify sustainable pathways for ocean-based food systems.
Representative topics: fisheries adaptation, food security, sustainable aquaculture, blue economy, ocean-climate-food nexus.

title: Research
text:
Ocean Sustainability and Biodiversity
Achieving sustainable oceans requires balancing biodiversity conservation with the needs of people. My research investigates how marine protected areas, ecosystem-based management, biodiversity policy, and nature-positive approaches can strengthen both ecological integrity and human well-being. I contribute to international assessments and collaborate with governments and organizations to translate science into policy.
Representative topics: biodiversity conservation, marine protected areas, ecosystem-based management, IPBES, global biodiversity policy.

title: Research
text:
Ocean Futures and Scenarios
Preparing for uncertain futures requires exploring multiple plausible pathways rather than predicting a single outcome. My research develops scenarios that combine climate projections, ecosystem models, socioeconomic change, and stakeholder knowledge to examine future risks, opportunities, and transformative solutions. Increasingly, this work focuses on tipping points, resilience, and pathways toward sustainable ocean futures.
Representative topics: future scenarios, tipping points, resilience, integrated assessment, participatory storylines, IPCC.

title: Projects
text:
TIP-BLUE

Tipping Points in Atlantic Marine Social-Ecological Systems
TIP-BLUE investigates how changes in Atlantic Ocean circulation, including the potential weakening of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC), could influence marine ecosystems, fisheries, coastal communities, and biodiversity. The project combines climate modelling, ecosystem modelling, participatory scenario development, and governance analysis to identify both risks and opportunities for building resilient ocean futures.
Role: Project Lead

title: Projects
text:
IPCC Seventh Assessment Report (AR7)
As Coordinating Lead Author for Chapter 12 (North America), I help coordinate the assessment of climate change impacts, risks, adaptation, and vulnerability across North America. The assessment synthesizes thousands of scientific studies to inform governments and society.
Role: Coordinating Lead Author

title: Training & Mentoring
text:
My Mentoring Philosophy
I encourage trainees to:

Develop strong quantitative and analytical skills.
Think across disciplines and scales.
Ask ambitious scientific questions.
Work collaboratively and respectfully.
Engage with policy and real-world decision making.
Communicate science effectively to diverse audiences.

My goal is not simply to supervise research projects, but to help researchers develop the confidence and skills needed for successful and fulfilling careers.

title: Training & Mentoring
text:
Working Together
Successful research depends on openness, trust, and shared purpose.
I seek to build a research culture where everyone contributes, learns from one another, and enjoys tackling important scientific questions together.

title: Leadership
text:
Research Leadership
My research brings together marine ecology, climate science, fisheries, economics, and social sciences to understand how ocean systems respond to environmental change. I have led international collaborations involving universities, governments, NGOs, and intergovernmental organizations across multiple continents.
Current leadership roles include major international research projects, interdisciplinary synthesis activities, and collaborative networks focused on climate change, biodiversity, and sustainable oceans.

title: Leadership
text:
Science for Policy
A central part of my work is ensuring that scientific knowledge informs decision-making.
I have contributed to major international assessments including the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) and the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES). These assessments synthesize the best available scientific evidence to support governments in addressing climate change, biodiversity loss, food security, and sustainable development.
Beyond formal assessments, I work closely with governments, international organizations, and non-governmental organizations to co-develop evidence that supports practical policy and management decisions.

title: Leadership
text:
Building Research Communities
Science advances through collaboration.
As former Director of the Institute for the Oceans and Fisheries at the University of British Columbia and founder of the Changing Ocean Research Unit (CORU), I have worked to create inclusive, interdisciplinary research environments where students, postdoctoral fellows, faculty, and partners can work together to tackle complex ocean challenges.
I believe that strong research communities are built on mutual respect, shared purpose, openness, and a commitment to scientific excellence.

title: Leadership
text:
Mentorship
One of the most rewarding aspects of my career is mentoring students and early-career researchers.
I encourage independent thinking, interdisciplinary collaboration, and engagement beyond academia. Many former students and postdoctoral fellows now hold academic, government, and international leadership positions around the world.
Mentorship is not only about developing technical expertise—it is about helping researchers become thoughtful, collaborative, and impactful scientific leaders.

title: Leadership
text:
Looking Forward
The challenges facing the ocean require science that is internationally connected, interdisciplinary, solution-oriented, and relevant to society.
I aim to contribute to a future in which scientific knowledge helps build resilient marine ecosystems, sustainable blue food systems, and equitable ocean governance for generations to come.

title: Knowledge Mobilization
text:
International Assessments
I contribute to major international scientific assessments that synthesize the best available evidence for global decision-making.
These include:

Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)
Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES)
United Nations initiatives on sustainable oceans and biodiversity

These assessments provide independent scientific advice that supports governments worldwide.

title: Knowledge Mobilization
text:
Working with Decision Makers
Many research projects are developed jointly with government agencies, international organizations, NGOs, and industry partners.
Rather than communicating results only after research is completed, I seek to co-produce knowledge by engaging partners throughout project design, implementation, interpretation, and application.

title: Knowledge Mobilization
text:
Tools for Decision Support
My research develops practical tools that help evaluate future risks and opportunities under climate change.
These include:

Marine ecosystem models
Fisheries and food security assessments
Climate risk analyses
Future scenarios and storylines
Biodiversity and conservation planning tools

These approaches help decision-makers explore alternative futures and evaluate adaptation options before major changes occur.

title: Knowledge Mobilization
text:
Public Engagement
I regularly communicate scientific findings through invited lectures, public presentations, media interviews, and workshops.
I believe that improving ocean sustainability requires dialogue among scientists, policymakers, practitioners, Indigenous knowledge holders, industry, and society.

title: Knowledge Mobilization
text:
From Knowledge to Action
The goal of knowledge mobilization is not simply to communicate research results—it is to enable better decisions.
By combining scientific excellence with collaboration and engagement, I aim to contribute to resilient marine ecosystems, sustainable blue food systems, and evidence-informed ocean governance.
